objects.taxonomy_description: Time-telling device designed for wall mounting with a circular face 20-40 cm in diameter. Face features hour numerals (Arabic, Roman, or markers) arranged in a 12-hour circle. Two or three hands (hour, minute, second) rotate from the center. Frame is wood, metal, or plastic in various finishes (oak, black, white, brass). Mounting bracket or keyhole slot on the back. Quartz movement powered by a single AA battery. Glass or plastic crystal covers the face. Some models have a pendulum visible below the face. Overall depth is 5-10 cm.

objects.taxonomy_description: Large shepherd dog with a medium-length double coat in black-and-tan, sable, or solid black. Coat is dense, straight, and close-lying with a thick undercoat. Body is athletic, well-muscled, and slightly longer than tall with a distinctive sloping topline. Head is noble and clean-cut with a broad skull and long, strong muzzle. Ears are large, erect, pointed, and set high. Tail is bushy, reaches to the hock, and carried low with a slight curve. Eyes are medium-sized, almond-shaped, and dark brown with an intelligent, alert expression. The breed's signature features include its erect ears, sloping back, and noble, wolf-like appearance.

objects.taxonomy_description: Medium-sized freshwater to brackish water turtle measuring 12-25 cm in carapace length. Carapace is oval and moderately domed with a smooth surface; coloration varies from brown to olive with concentric growth rings visible on each scute. Some species exhibit ornate patterning with yellow or orange markings on dark scutes. Plastron is large and hinged, enabling partial closure. Head is moderately sized with a pointed snout and small eyes; skin coloration is grey to olive with distinctive striped or spotted patterning on the head and neck. Limbs are moderately long with webbed feet and sharp claws. Tail is short. The turtle exhibits a characteristic basking posture on logs or banks with limbs extended and head raised. Skin texture is smooth with fine scales. Adapted for both aquatic and terrestrial environments, spending significant time basking to regulate body temperature.
